news_drafts.headline: North Essex Parking Partnership forecasts £223k surplus for year ending March 2027, £174k ahead of £49k budget
news_drafts.lead: The North Essex Parking Partnership, run jointly by Colchester and other councils, is on track to deliver a £223,000 surplus for the year ending March 2027, exceeding its budgeted surplus of £49,000 by £174,000. The outperformance is driven largely by penalty charge notice income running £100,000 ahead of forecast, reflecting strong enforcement performance through August. Additional unbudgeted income of £72,000 from traffic regulation order work for other authorities and Essex County Council has also contributed. The partnership's reserve is forecast to grow to £615,000 by March, £174,000 above plan. However, the council has budgeted for only a 2.5 per cent salary increase while the national pay award for local government has moved to 3.3 per cent; if Colchester negotiates a higher local rate, it would create additional financial pressure. The council has also noted uncertainty over the operational timelines of its fee structure, set through March 2030, following the halt to Essex Local Government Reorganisation.

findings.headline: Partnership reserve building faster than planned: forecast to reach £615k by March 2027, £174k above budget
findings.detail: Opening reserve balance at 1 April 2026 was £392k. Budgeted closing balance (with £49k surplus) was £441k; forecast closing balance (with £223k surplus) is £615k. Reserve growth is therefore £174k above plan, signalling either over-contribution from councils or under-spending assumptions relative to budget.
findings.matters: Faster reserve accumulation suggests the partnership's pricing or cost assumptions were overly conservative; significant reserves provide financial resilience but may need to be deployed or reflected in reduced charges to partner councils or users.
findings.figures: Opening balance £392k; budgeted closing £441k; forecast closing £615k; increase of £174k above plan
findings.quote: However, based on the current forecast surplus of £223k, the Reserve balance is projected to increase to £615k by 31st March 2027, representing an increase of £174k above the budgeted position.

findings.headline: Pay award inflation moved from 2.5% budget assumption to 3.3% mid-year, with further risk if council negotiates higher rate
findings.detail: Budget assumed 2.5% pay award. Following NJC agreement of 3.3% local government pay award, the partnership updated its forecast to 3.3%. However, Colchester City Council negotiates pay locally and has not yet agreed its 2026/27 rate. The paper explicitly flags that if CCC agrees a rate higher than 3.3%, it will create 'additional in-year financial pressure above that currently reflected within the forecast.'
findings.matters: This flags a real mid-year cost pressure that was not in the original budget; it shows the partnership is exposed to further pay award inflation beyond the 3.3% now assumed, creating unquantified budget uncertainty.
findings.figures: Pay award assumption increased from 2.5% to 3.3%; potential for further increase if CCC negotiates locally
findings.quote: However, should CCC ultimately agree a local pay award higher than 3.3%, this would create an ad ditional in -year financial pressure above that currently reflected within the forecast, which will need to be managed through future monitoring reports.

findings.headline: £72k of full-year income forecast comes from unbudgeted ad hoc Traffic Regulation Order work not in base budget
findings.detail: Partnership reports £58k YTD and £72k full-year forecast over-recovery from ad hoc TRO work undertaken for other local authorities and Essex County Council. The paper explicitly states this work is not included in the base budget, so these additional works are unbudgeted windfall income with no guarantee of recurrence.
findings.matters: This income source is not part of the partnership's core operating model and may not recur at this level; future budgets should not assume this income, and the council should understand that base-case sustainability is lower than the positive variance suggests.
findings.quote: £58k over-recovery of income across other areas. This is primarily attributable to ad hoc Traffic Regulation Order (TRO) work undertaken on behalf of local authorities and Essex County Council. As this work is not included within the base budget, any additional works generate unbudgeted income, which has been reflected in the forecast.

findings.headline: Penalty Charge Notice income £100k ahead of forecast, driven by strong enforcement performance
findings.detail: PCN income shows year-to-date over-recovery of £92k with full-year forecast over-recovery of £100k. The paper notes performance remains strong based on actual results to end of August. This is the single largest driver of the partnership's variance to budget.
findings.matters: Strong PCN collection demonstrates effective enforcement operations, but also shows budget assumptions were materially conservative; if enforcement effectiveness or market conditions soften, income would revert sharply.
findings.quote: £92k over-recovery of Penalty Charge Notice (PCN) income. Performance remains strong based on income received to the end of August and this improved position has been reflected in the full-year forecast.

findings.headline: Partnership forecast to deliver £223k surplus, £174k ahead of £49k budget
findings.detail: Year-to-date position at August 2026 shows a £222k surplus, forecast to reach £223k for the full year, exceeding the budgeted surplus of £49k by £174k. The outperformance is driven by £172k income over-recovery, partially offset by £2.5k expenditure underspend.
findings.matters: Material outperformance suggests budgets were conservative or operations performed better than expected; this affects reserve building and the council's financial position as a partnership stakeholder.
findings.figures: £222k YTD surplus; £223k forecast surplus; £49k budgeted surplus; £174k variance
findings.quote: The forecast outturn position for 2026/27, presented in Appendix A, is expected to provide a year-end surplus of £223k, which is £174k above the 2026/27 budgeted surplus of £49k.
